alignment_method: hybrid: tfidf shortlist -> grade+keyword rerank -> LLM curation (Claude Sonnet)
notes: High-school argumentative mini-essay on heroism in The Odyssey (introduction + single body paragraph).

objectives.title: GradeFlow Intro
objectives.note: Logistical / platform onboarding. No ELA standard applies.

objectives.title: MLA Heading
objectives.description: Create MLA heading (name, teacher, class, date) at top-left.

alignments.rationale: Producing writing appropriate to task and purpose touches format conventions, though MLA heading itself is largely logistical.

objectives.title: Essay Title
objectives.description: Draft a title that tells the reader what the essay is about.

alignments.rationale: Writing a title tied to task and purpose falls under producing clear and coherent writing.

objectives.title: Prewriting — Introduction
objectives.description: Plan hook, background, thesis via a prewriting table.

alignments.rationale: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing — prewriting is the 'planning' phase.
Introduce precise claim(s), distinguish from alternate claims, and create organization — the intro/thesis frame.

objectives.title: Prewriting — Topic and Commentary
objectives.description: Plan topic sentence, evidence, and commentary for the body paragraph.

alignments.rationale: Planning body-paragraph structure is part of the writing process.
Develop claims and counterclaims fairly, supplying evidence for each.

objectives.title: Prewriting — Commentary and Conclusion
objectives.description: Plan additional evidence and commentary through to the conclusion.

alignments.rationale: Planning stage of the writing process.
Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument.

objectives.title: Insert Section Breaks
objectives.description: Insert Section Break (continuous) for GradeFlow identification.
objectives.note: Platform-specific document formatting. No ELA standard applies.

objectives.title: Introduction Paragraph
objectives.description: Write hook, background, and a main argument. Must include required elements.

alignments.rationale: Write arguments to support claims with valid reasoning — the overarching argument-writing standard.
Introduce precise claim(s) and create an organization that establishes clear relationships among claim(s), counterclaims, reasons, and evidence.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph
objectives.description: Topic sentence, two quoted pieces of evidence, commentary, conclusion.

alignments.rationale: Develop claim(s) fairly, supplying evidence for each while pointing out strengths and limitations.
Use words, phrases, and clauses to link the major sections of the text, create cohesion, and clarify relationships.
Cite strong and thorough textual evidence to support analysis — the quote-selection and quote-handling part.

objectives.title: Prewriting Connections
objectives.description: Review that prewriting plan flows into final essay (quotes and commentary).

alignments.rationale: Revising to ensure the plan is reflected — editing/revising phase of writing.

objectives.title: Introduction Paragraph (Teacher Graded)
objectives.description: Verify hook, title/author, summary, and directional thesis.

alignments.rationale: Introduce precise claim(s) and establish significance — this is the thesis-and-framing check.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph (Teacher Graded)
objectives.description: Clear topic sentence, two quotes, commentary on Odysseus's heroism.

alignments.rationale: Develop claim(s) and supply evidence — graded on quote integration and support.
Analyze how complex characters (Odysseus) develop and advance themes (heroism).

objectives.title: Quality and Format
objectives.description: Analytical language, smooth flow, commentary starters, MLA format.

alignments.rationale: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline.
Apply knowledge of language to make effective choices — vary sentence structure for meaning and style.
Conventions of standard English grammar and usage in the polished draft.
